evals.expected_output: A Conventional Commits message typed after the dominant change (e.g. `fix(parser): handle empty input` or `chore: ...`). Subject is imperative, lowercase, no trailing period, ≤72 chars. No invented scope when changes span unrelated areas; agent suggests splitting if the diff mixes cleanly separable work.
assertions: Commit message follows `<type>(<optional scope>): <subject>` shape with a recognized type (feat/fix/docs/refactor/perf/test/build/ci/chore/style/revert)
Subject is in imperative mood and lowercase with no trailing period
No unnecessary body/footer sections added for a trivial change

evals.prompt: I just rewrote our storage layer to use async iterators instead of the old callback API — the public SDK methods Storage.read() and Storage.write() are gone. we're about to cut a release. write the commit message.
evals.expected_output: `feat(storage)!:` (or `refactor(storage)!:`) subject plus a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer naming the removed methods and how to migrate. The `!` and footer appear together.
assertions: Message starts with a type followed by an exclamation mark before the colon (e.g. feat(storage)!:/refactor(storage)!:) signaling a breaking change
A BREAKING CHANGE: footer is present describing what broke or how to migrate
Scope reflects the affected area (storage) and subject stays imperative and concise

evals.prompt: squash these three wip commits into one proper commit. they all fix the crash that happened when uploading files bigger than 2gb
evals.expected_output: A single squashed commit with message like `fix(upload): handle files larger than 2GB`, imperative subject, optional body explaining the cause. Not `fix: wip` style residue.
assertions: Squash results in exactly one commit whose message uses the `fix` type with a meaningful imperative subject
Subject references the actual bug (large file upload crash), not 'wip' or 'various fixes'
No leftover empty placeholder sections in the message

evals.prompt: our team history uses kernel-style messages like `net: drop redundant checksum` and `mm: simplify page reclaim` — check the log to confirm. then commit my staged changes (they tweak the retry loop in the scheduler). follow our house style, not any generic convention.
evals.expected_output: Agent inspects git log, recognizes the established non-Conventional-Commits style, and writes e.g. `sched: tune retry loop backoff`. It does NOT force a conventional-commits prefix onto this repo.
assertions: Agent checked recent git log before writing the message
Final message matches the repo's existing `subsystem: summary` style rather than conventional-commits format
Message still follows universal good practice (imperative, concise, no trailing period)
